title: Champions vs native Ascend aclnn (CANN 9.0.0), measured 2026-11-07

protocol.pypto_side: frozen remote_harness.py (sha256 5c7b7aa4... identical across all domain verifiers and /root/ptocontri/pkg), latency_us = median per-round effective_us (PYPTO_BENCH=1)
protocol.aclnn_side: tools/aclnn_bench.py (pyacl + ctypes on libopapi.so): wall-clock per round (enqueue aclnn call(s) + acl.rt.synchronize_stream), median; aclnn executor fetched once via *GetWorkspaceSize, marked repeatable, reused across rounds. Both sides are end-to-end wall clock including host dispatch.
protocol.shape_policy: primary = champion's native decision preset {M:512, N:1024, bf16} (s-tier campaign); secondary = public-support maximum corner {M:1152, N:2048}; m-tier {M:4096,N:4096} attempted and recorded

aclnn_baseline_semantics: No single aclnn op implements exact symmetric per-token dynamic INT8 quant, so the native baseline is the unfused decomposition a user writes: aclnnAbs -> aclnnAmax(dim=-1, keepdim) -> aclnnCast(fp32) -> aclnnDivs(127) [=scale] -> aclnnCast(fp32) -> aclnnDiv(broadcast scale) -> aclnnRound -> aclnnClamp(-127,127) -> aclnnCast(int8) [=q]. abs/amax are exact in bf16 so the bf16-then-cast order is bit-identical to cast-then-reduce; scale output matches our fp32 golden to 1.9e-9. No all-zero-row guard (probability-0 under randn; a guard would add an aclnnWhere stage). KNOWN DIVERGENCE: aclnnDiv is not bit-identical to torch fp32 division, so exact .5 ties in the quotient round differently in ~0.02-0.03% of elements (off by exactly one count, e.g. 63.5 -> 63 instead of RNE 64); aclnnRound itself is RNE (probed: 63.5->64, -63.5->-64, 0.5->0). q check therefore passes at rtol=0/atol=1 with n_mismatch recorded; scale is effectively exact.

results.aclnn_q_mismatch: 110 / 524288 elements (0.021%), all off-by-one at exact .5 quotient ties (aclnnDiv ulp divergence, see semantics note); scale exact to 1.9e-9
724 / 2359296 elements (0.031%), same off-by-one tie pattern; scale exact to 1.9e-9
